newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish police detain Islamist protesters.
newsitem.headline: Turkish police detain Islamist protesters.

text.p: Turkish police on Friday detained around 20 people at an Islamist demonstration against government plans to curb Moslem religious education, witnesses said.
"You can't stop the Islamic movement," hundreds of protesters chanted outside the 16th Century Beyazit mosque after noon prayers.

Police equipped with helmets and plastic body armour -- known locally as "robocops" -- broke up the protest and chased the Islamists up sidestreets. Two police minibuses later took detainees away from the area.
Security had been tight at large mosques throughout Turkey following a demonstration in Ankara earlier in the week that turned ugly.

Eleven people, mostly journalists, were wounded on Tuesday when police baton-charged thousands of Islamists in the capital protesting against a government bid to extand secularist education at the expense of Islamic secondary schools.
Police body-searched worshippers going into Ankara's main Kocatepe mosque for Friday prayers.
Uniformed and plainclothes police milled around the Grand Mosque in Diyarbakir, the main city in the mainly Kurdish southeast.
Islamist anger at Turkey's secularist establishment has risen since Islamist Pime Minister Necmettin Erbakan resigned under military pressure in June. He was replaced by secularist Mesut Yilmaz.
A car bomb exploded in central Turkey on Friday in an apparent attempt to free eight Islamist convicts being carried to court in an armoured prison vehicle, Anatolian news agency said.
It said three gendarmerie police and an inmate were wounded in the attack in Kirsehir province.
